title: TCU's Alice robot flags DNIT notices for BR-153 maintenance on stretches already under concession; TCU Acórdão 1116/2017 cancels the tender
summary: Alice flagged DNIT Goiás notices for BR-153 maintenance on concession stretches (R$39m per Inforchannel); TCU Acórdão 1116/2017 canceled the R$20m tender (JOTA).
account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice and auction record published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It had been running for about ten months when TCU presented it at a TCU–CGU data-analysis seminar on 25–26 September 2017. Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. A JOTA article of 22 November 2017 states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. The two sources give different numbers of notices and amounts. The acórdão itself was not available. The decision date is not reported.
purpose: Daily automated screening of federal tender notices for signs of irregularity so that auditors can act during the public phase of a tender. This use was its intended purpose.
system: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais), TCU/CGU text-analysis and data cross-checking robot
developer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) with the Ministério da Transparência e Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), in-house
deployer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), Goiás unit
domain: Public administration: external audit and procurement control
segment: Federal court of accounts (anti-waste and anti-corruption control)

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary is identified in either source.

Material to DNIT and TCU: both cited sources state that the tender(s) were blocked or canceled by acórdão after the Alice alert. The amount is given as R$39 million (two notices) by Inforchannel and R$20 million (one notice) by JOTA.
A single highway tender among some 60,000 federal tenders a year, small at national scale.

ai_role.statement: Alice's role was detection. Per Inforchannel it pulls the estimated value from notice text, runs nine text analyses for competitiveness restrictions and 23 database cross-checks. The auditor's statement and the JOTA article attribute the discovery of the BR-153 notices to Alice. The cancellation was a decision of the TCU plenary (Acórdão 1116/2017). Both sources rest on TCU staff statements, the deployer describing its own in-house tool. The source counts as independent because TCU is a public body, not a vendor. The acórdão text was not obtained, so the two accounts' differing figures (R$39 million, two notices; R$20 million, one notice) cannot be reconciled.

produced_by: Daily collection of all tender notices and auction records from Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União
Rule-based text analysis (nine checks on competitiveness restrictions, reading of estimated value) and 23 database cross-checks of suppliers
Auditors in the TCU Goiás unit reading the alerts during the public phase of the tender
A TCU plenary decision (acórdão) within two months of the alert
must_hold: Notices published on Comprasnet in machine-readable text
Alerts reaching auditors within the 15–30-day public phase
Auditors with capacity to open a case or contact the contracting body
Contracting bodies or the court willing to block or cancel flawed tenders

headline: TCU's Alice flags DNIT's BR-153 notices; TCU cancels the tender
metric: ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million

comparator.against: TCU auditors reading the roughly 200 federal tender notices published each day by hand
comparator.before: seria muito custoso porque são, em média, 200 editais por dia
comparator.after: Os auditores do Tribunal de Contas da União recebem pontualmente às 19h um e-mail de Alice. São os resumos das centenas de contratações federais publicadas naquele dia.
comparator.quote: “Esse tipo de trabalho poderia ser feito por humanos, mas seria muito custoso porque são, em média, 200 editais por dia”, diz Wesley Vaz Silva, diretor da Secretaria de Fiscalização de Tecnologia da Informação do TCU, ao G1.

later.note: By March 2018 G1 reported that Alice, Sofia and Monica were also in use at the CGU, the Federal Prosecution Service, the Federal Police and state courts of accounts, and that flawed tenders had been canceled after their tips.
later.quote: As três robôs já são usadas por servidores da Controladoria Geral da União, Ministério Público Federal, Polícia Federal e tribunais de contas dos Estados. Depois de dicas delas, licitações com falhas já foram canceladas e compras públicas enviesadas tiveram que ser refeitas.

fields.account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice and auction record published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It had been running for about ten months when TCU presented it at a TCU–CGU data-analysis seminar on 25–26 September 2017. Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. A JOTA article of 22 November 2017 states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. The two sources give different numbers of notices and amounts. The acórdão itself was not available. The decision date is not reported.

fields.account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice and auction record published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It had been running for about ten months when TCU presented it at a TCU–CGU data-analysis seminar on 25–26 September 2017. Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. A JOTA article of 22 November 2017 states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. The two sources give different numbers of notices and amounts. The acórdão itself was not available. The decision date is not reported.
